$comment: The ANSWER contract for fleet_ssh. parse.schema.json governs the INPUT (utterance -> scope/cols); this governs the OUTPUT (the table the user actually reads). Both are needed: a correct parse that renders a lying table is still a wrong answer. LIMIT, MEASURED: JSON Schema validates STRUCTURE only. A table that collapses (unreachable) into "-", or that silently drops a box row, BOTH VALIDATE against this file -- and those are the two ways a fleet sweep actually lies. table-bench.sh carries those as explicit checks; do not mistake schema conformance for a correct table.

header.description: Column names, in order. Element 0 is ALWAYS the literal "BOX"; every later element is one thing the user asked for, matching parse.schema.json's cols count.

rows.description: One row per box in SCOPE, in the order the boxes were given or discovered. Never fewer rows than boxes: a box that failed still gets a row.

box.description: The box name, i.e. column BOX.

cells.description: One cell per header column after BOX, same order. THREE DISTINCT STATES, never collapsed: a value (the command answered), "-" (the box answered but the command produced no output), or "(unreachable)" (the box never answered). Collapsing these is how a fleet sweep lies -- "ssh failed" and "printed nothing" need different fixes.

unreachable.description: True when the box never answered. In the rendered table "(unreachable)" appears ONCE, in the first data column, not repeated per column: it is a fact about the box, not about each field.
